records.reporting_boundary_basis: WETREP applies to every kind of oil tanker of more than 600 tonnes deadweight carrying heavy crude oil, heavy fuel oil or bitumen and tar (MSC.190(79) annex para 1.1): tanker-specific. Its north-eastern limit is the straight line from point 19 (51 22'25"N 003 21'52".5E) to point 20 (52 12'N UK east coast, about 001 37'E), confirmed on the chartlet (P-S5). Testing the Circ.67 positions (P-S1) against that line: all south-western and central positions (79, 80, 83, 84, 86) are 25-56' of longitude inside; the north-eastern corner positions (81, 82, 85, 87) lie within about 1-2' of the line (on it within plotting precision). Effectively the whole scheme is inside WETREP, with the NE extremity on the boundary. Outside CALDOVREP (P-S19).
records.evidence_summary: Inside the WETREP (VRS-0005) reporting area on the Part I boundary coordinates (near-full; NE end on the limit line). Applies to heavy-grade oil tankers only. No VTS coverage established; outside Rotterdam and (per 2014 chart) Scheldt VTS areas.

records.vts_boundary_basis: The VTS area at sea is the territorial sea within a 12 nm radius of the IJmuiden breakwater heads, including the extended IJ-geul (P-S12); the statutory IJmuiden approach area uses a 12 nm arc from reference point 52 27'.9N 004 32'.1E (P-S10). IJmuiden West Inner spans 004 07'-004 20'.35E (Circ.64, P-S2). Its eastern end (e.g. (16) 52 30'.52N 004 20'.35E, about 7.6 nm) lies inside 12 nm; the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme near 004 12'.6E, so roughly the eastern 4-5 nm (less if the territorial-sea limit is tighter) is inside and the western part is outside. Partial.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system (P-S6); outside WETREP (P-S5). No Dutch reporting system under STZ art. 5a or the EEZ regulation was found (P-S10, P-S17). Arrival report at 12 nm to Sector IJmuiden VHF 61 and the report to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 'as soon as VHF contact is possible' are VTS / port-approach duties of the same authority (P-S12), not a separate MRS.
records.evidence_summary: Eastern portion of IJmuiden West Inner lies inside the 12 nm VTS area of the North Sea Canal Area (Sector IJmuiden, VHF 61); western portion outside, in the information-only IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7) area. No mandatory reporting scheme.

records.unresolved_issue: Exact split point depends on whether the 12 nm is measured from the breakwater heads or the STZ reference point and on the territorial-sea limit; partial coverage itself is not in doubt. Name of the traffic centre not stated in the regulation.

method_notes: Accessed 29 September 2026. IMO baseline geometry from COLREG.2/Circ.67 (B-II/10, in force 1 June 2017), Circ.64 (B-II/11, 1 August 2013), Circ.66/Corr.1 (Off Friesland, 1 June 2015); circulars read from third-party mirrors because imo.org circulars and NOAA copies were blocked. Distances computed by plane approximation (cos latitude) from the North Mole head (Rotterdam) and the STZ IJmuiden reference point; WETREP side-of-line test treats the 19-20 limit as a straight line in latitude/longitude with the UK east-coast point at about 001 37'E (sensitivity 001 35'-001 40'E reported). Dutch statutes read from wetten.overheid.nl current versions; Staatscourant via officielebekendmakingen.nl SRU. Rotterdam 2026 procedure is image-only PDF: read visually (pages rendered); the sector chart is schematic, so VTS coverage of the Maas schemes rests on the combination of the chart and the PIG '38 nm' service-area statement, and the statutory approach area (Maas Centre precautionary area) is noted as smaller. defensie.nl NtM links in the old 'binaries/defensie/verzamelingen' path return 404; the working path is www.defensie.nl/site/binaries/site-content/collections/baz-weekly-editions/<year>/<week>/<file>.pdf. EU VTMIS (Directive 2002/59/EC) port-bound notifications are not TSS-specific and were not treated as MRS. Not checked: ALRS Vol 6 (not accessible), current Belgian/UK VTS lists, German Bight Traffic limits for East Friesland. No repository files edited.
